summary: The brief's mechanism is falsified by measurement: every failing lock passes id 0x00000000 to _sys_lwmutex_lock, not the structure address 0x0165afc8, and control+16 IS written -- by the lifted firmware wrapper at 0.844 s, 246 ms AFTER the lock burst. The guest structure is BSS zero-fill; its lock word is held (1) while sleep_queue is still 0, i.e. a mutex taken through the fast path before any create. RPCS3 returns the same CELL_ESRCH for id 0 (sys_lwmutex.cpp:191), so the ESRCH is the console's own answer. The real defects found against RPCS3 were in create(): no protocol validation (minted an object for ANY protocol and returned CELL_OK) and has_name read backwards (RPCS3 :41 keeps the name only when has_name is NEGATIVE; ours kept it for any non-zero). Both fixed. tests/lwmutex_create.cpp drives the REAL handler through a forwarder: red 9 failures without the fix, green 0 with it. Final counts from the syscall dispatcher, not one module: 881 ESRCH, all _sys_lwmutex_lock, 0 EPERM; +0x60 = 0x00000000. Rebased on main f364124, git diff --diff-filter=D is empty, 38/38 ctest pass on the rebased tree, and the clean run is 661 flips -- exactly main's recorded baseline.
